persons.name: Amelia
persons.harm: Her husband, in active opioid and later methamphetamine addiction, subjected her to escalating emotional abuse, night-time harassment, phone stalking, a gun-store threat and a shrine, pushed her and threw a toy at her face, took their son for a $5,000 ransom, and finally broke in and set their home on fire.
persons.perpetrator_role: her ex-husband

contacts.when: after the chainsaw incident; repeated calls (8-10 times)
contacts.what_was_asked: help stopping night-time harassment and threats; building a record for custody
contacts.what_institution_did: Officers came but each time said nothing could be done unless he physically assaulted her.
contacts.quote: The police would come and they would say until he physically assaults you, there's nothing we can do.
contacts.what_happened_next: Harassment and stalking escalated.
contacts.notes: Recurring response; she later says 'The cops had been to our house like eight or 10 times by now.'

contacts.when: after he pushed her and threw a toy that hit her face
contacts.what_institution_did: Said it sounded like assault but without visible marks they could do nothing.
contacts.quote: I called the police and told them what happened. They said it sounds like assault but we don't see any physical marks so we can't do anything.
contacts.what_happened_next: No action; stalking continued.

contacts.institution: phone company (carrier) and its security team
contacts.what_was_asked: remove him from the account / stop him tracking her phone
contacts.what_institution_did: Tried repeatedly to shut off his line; security could not stop him reversing it.
contacts.quote: was doing and they said this guy is good. We don't know how he's getting through all these walls, we keep shutting his phone off and he keeps turning it back on and we don't know how he's doing it.
contacts.what_happened_next: He kept service and taunted her.

contacts.when: after he dropped a gun-store pin and threatening texts
contacts.what_was_asked: protection after a perceived death threat
contacts.what_institution_did: Held him outside so she could collect belongings; on seeing the shrine said it was crazy but not illegal and took no further action.
contacts.quote: And he said, oh, it's definitely crazy, but crazy is not illegal. We can't do anything.
contacts.what_happened_next: She left to stay with a friend.
contacts.notes: Escort step ('we'll hold him outside and you go in and you get your things') shown at 16:32; also did_nothing on the threat itself.

contacts.institution: police called by her workplace security
contacts.when: the morning he came to her workplace
contacts.what_was_asked: work security called because of how he was parked/behaving
contacts.what_institution_did: Police spoke with him and then with her; she told them about the situation; no action shown.
contacts.quote: And then the police come in and start talking to me about what's going on. And I fill them in on the chaos that our life has become.
contacts.what_happened_next: He drove to the daycare and took their son.

contacts.what_was_asked: call her if he arrived for the boys
contacts.what_institution_did: The director was about to call her when he arrived; could not stop him taking the child.
contacts.quote: the director of the daycare has the phone in her handage that I was just about to call you.
contacts.what_happened_next: He took the boy, unrestrained, and demanded $5,000.

contacts.when: same day, after the son was taken and ransom demanded
contacts.what_institution_did: Dispatched a helicopter and told her to get a restraining order.
contacts.quote: I told that to the police and they dispatched a helicopter to try to find the car.
contacts.what_happened_next: She went to court; the boy was returned by him at midnight.

contacts.what_institution_did: A clerk recognised it as domestic violence and the judge granted an ex parte order requiring him to leave the house.
contacts.quote: He's like, yeah, it was granted. Basically saying he has to leave the house immediately.
contacts.what_happened_next: Order not effective until served.
contacts.notes: Clerk: 'that's domestic violence' (24:48).

contacts.what_institution_did: Two deputies served the order on the spot and removed him; warned him he would go to jail if he returned.
contacts.quote: He said, this is a restraining order. You need to vacate the premises immediately.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was later arrested for a meth DUI (deputy informed her).

contacts.what_institution_did: Ordered him to stay away from the home but allowed visitation monitored by his mother; she then dropped the order with those stipulations.
contacts.quote: The judge basically said that he still had to stay away from the home and he was still not allowed in our residence,
contacts.what_happened_next: Days later he broke in and set the house on fire.

contacts.what_was_asked: 911 calls by his mother and neighbours
contacts.what_institution_did: SWAT standoff, arrest, and an emergency protective order for her with victim notification registration.
contacts.quote: I was told because I got an emergency protective order from the sheriffs that night. You can register for a phone call that basically alerts you when there's a change in status if you're a victim of a crime
contacts.what_happened_next: He was released on bail; she went into hiding.

contacts.what_institution_did: Police escorted her to a women's shelter, which took her and her sons in; she left after two days.
contacts.quote: So I packed up the room and we went to a women's shelter. You follow the police car and they take you to the women's shelter.
contacts.what_happened_next: She left because 'it was not the environment that I wanted my boys in.'

contacts.institution: police department of the city she was hiding in (detective)
contacts.what_was_asked: his former employer requested a threat assessment
contacts.what_institution_did: Detective did a threat assessment and added patrols around her hotel.
contacts.quote: the detective said, we're going to do some extra patrols around the hotel you're staying in to make sure that you're safe.

contacts.what_institution_did: Ordered a custody evaluation and limited him to visitation monitored by his parents.
contacts.quote: What was decided was that he could have monitored visitation by his parents, by his step-on and dad.

contacts.what_institution_did: Convicted him of felony arson, breaking and entering and vandalism; one year in a 'pay and stay' jail plus probation.
contacts.quote: Ultimately, he was convicted of felony arson, breaking an entering and vandalism for all of that. He received one year of jail time with eligibility for a pay and stay jail if he could afford it, which he could.
contacts.what_happened_next: She felt the sentence was unfair; three years' probation followed.
contacts.notes: Victim impact statement given.

contacts.what_institution_did: Judge said he questioned her judgment for dropping the first restraining order.
contacts.quote: The judge basically reprimanded me for dropping that first restraining order, and my house was burned down three days later.

contacts.when: after his parents took the boys out of the county
contacts.what_institution_did: Judge terminated his visitation.
contacts.quote: So we called him into court and the judge terminated visitation.
contacts.what_happened_next: Visitation later rebuilt in court-supervised steps.

persons.outcome_quote: my life is blissfully predictable. I know what my house looks like when I open that door every day.
persons.decisive_work_quote: Ultimately, he was convicted of felony arson, breaking an entering and vandalism for all of that.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: ex parte restraining order granted the day of the abduction, after 8-10 police calls that produced nothing
persons.notes: Medical/rehab contacts in E1 concern his addiction, not harm to her, and are not coded. The meth DUI arrest (deputy phoned her) is noted but not coded as a contact. Insurance company covered the arson loss because she had the restraining order (not coded). Harm ended through arrest, protective orders, conviction and court-controlled visitation; the judge's reprimand makes harmed_by_institution_ever true. She also documented with photos and texts for the ex parte order.

contacts.what_was_asked: call his mother if his father came
contacts.what_institution_did: Director was about to call; could not stop the father.
contacts.quote: the director of the daycare has the phone in her handage that I was just about to call you.
contacts.what_happened_next: He was taken.

contacts.what_institution_did: Dispatched a helicopter; advised a restraining order.
contacts.quote: I told that to the police and they dispatched a helicopter to try to find the car.
contacts.what_happened_next: Father returned him at midnight.

contacts.what_institution_did: Monitored visitation; terminated visitation when the order was breached.
contacts.quote: So we called him into court and the judge terminated visitation.

persons.outcome_quote: But the court is there to work in the best interest of the kids. And luckily he rose up, did the work to actually be a good functioning parent for the boys.
persons.decisive_work_quote: So we called him into court and the judge terminated visitation.
persons.notes: Told through his mother. Younger brother also affected but not separately followed.

persons.name: Odessa
persons.harm: Her husband, a youth pastor, pressured her into lengthy sex that injured her repeatedly, initiated sex while she was asleep, lied about pornography, had affairs including with a former youth-group student, and drained her savings while she was pregnant.
persons.perpetrator_role: her husband, a youth pastor

quotes.quote: Did you see this as sexual abuse at the time? No. I literally thought of it as my job.

because everybody I knew was so heavily steeped in the church, getting an enolment or even advising that I seek out couples counseling was not something that anybody would ever recommend to do. It was like, pray about it.

contacts.what_institution_did: Told her to refrain from sex for a while after she was injured.
contacts.quote: there was a few times where I did get pretty decently injured and I was told by my doctor that I needed to reframe from having sex for a while.
contacts.what_happened_next: The advice gave her a reason to refuse; abuse resumed later.
contacts.notes: Doctor saw sex-related injuries; whether the coercion was disclosed is not stated.

contacts.institution: her OB and hospital psychiatric/social services staff
contacts.when: when six months pregnant with her second child
contacts.what_institution_did: Hospitalized her for psychiatric evaluation; staff repeatedly asked if she was safe and offered security; arranged a therapist.
contacts.quote: I had so many people asking me if I was safe, if I needed an out, if I needed him to leave, if I needed security to help.
contacts.what_happened_next: She reassured them she was fine; they connected her to a therapist and medication.
contacts.notes: She declined the help offered.

contacts.what_institution_did: Told her she had to become his 'new drug' and be sexually available to cure his addiction.
contacts.quote: She looked at me and said, Odessa, if you want to help him get through this addiction, you're going to have to become his new drug, his new addiction.
contacts.what_happened_next: She agreed out of fear of losing the marriage.
contacts.notes: Placed responsibility on her and endangered her; her later therapist said this therapist 'was enabling your abuser'.

contacts.what_institution_did: Validated that the previous therapist enabled her abuser.
contacts.quote: she was like, your therapist was enabling your abuser.

persons.outcome_quote: I have self-worth now and self-confidence now that I don't think I ever would have had had I stayed in my marriage.
persons.notes: Harm ended because he left/she ended the marriage, not through an institution; no police or church report. Document: his eight-page letter partly read/paraphrased on air. Divorce lawyer (private) not coded.

persons.perpetrator_role: a man she dated long-distance after meeting on a dating app

quotes.quote: I still remember that line that his ID says that he's a woman. And because it says he's a woman that cops aren't going to give him the same amount of stress as if he was a bit.
a black man and not just a black man, a black trans man and putting that type of legal target. It didn't feel good.

contacts.what_institution_did: Listened, and connected her to a local shelter and legal aid.

contacts.institution: local domestic violence shelter and legal aid fellow
contacts.what_institution_did: Prepared and filed an emergency restraining order with her and later represented her in court.

contacts.when: about five days after calling the shelter
contacts.what_institution_did: Judge approved an emergency order.

contacts.what_was_asked: service of the order at his mother's address

contacts.quote: So the sheriff served him with the emergency restraining order and they made court.

contacts.what_happened_next: She has not heard from him since.

persons.decisive_work_quote: I knew I was doing the right thing and I refused the agreements because there was no legal protection for me if he decided to show up at my front door.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: about five days after she called the shelter
persons.notes: She found his prior DV restraining orders and jail record herself, located his mother's address for service, supplied screenshots and transcripts, and refused settlement. Friends suggested the hotline.

She also had a relationship with a married man who raged at her abortion. The perpetrators were never identified.

quotes.quote: I think that I have dissociative identity disorder. I'm reading all this stuff about it, and I'm like, oh my god, do I have another personality that's sending these emails?

contacts.when: when her cousin saw the Facebook posts
contacts.what_institution_did: Concluded someone was watching her and advised her to leave the city.
contacts.quote: And I told my therapist about it, he was like, whoever's doing this, they know where you are and what you're doing at your time's days.
contacts.what_happened_next: She moved to her parents' home.
contacts.notes: Also: 'My therapist was like, you need to leave the city.' (22:53)

contacts.what_was_asked: she half expected to turn herself in; help

contacts.what_institution_did: Went through IP addresses and emails and contacted everyone on her email list.

persons.outcome_quote: So there was really no resolution.

quotes.quote: I should have called the cops, but I didn't. I was like, you know what, this is just another one of those bad guys that you ran into.
I was scared to call the cops because cops are scary.

contacts.when: about a month after the assault, after an attempted break-in

contacts.quote: And so I reported that and the complex didn't do anything about it. They were like, okay, whatever.
contacts.what_happened_next: A second break-in attempt followed.

contacts.what_institution_did: Told her they could do nothing and to call police.

contacts.what_happened_next: She called police.

contacts.what_happened_next: He disappeared; never arrested.

contacts.what_institution_did: Refused; she was told she could only get one after another in-person encounter.
contacts.quote: I asked for a restraining order and I was not allowed to get one. I tried multiple ways. I submitted to the court the proper way that you're supposed to do it.
contacts.notes: Legal threshold, not disbelief, as told.

contacts.when: after she learned he was a con man

contacts.what_institution_did: He was told to leave when he appeared.

persons.name: Whitney
persons.harm: Abducted as a one-day-old newborn from a hospital nursery in Oklahoma City in June 1990 by a woman posing as a nurse, and kept for 11 days.
persons.perpetrator_role: a 19-year-old woman, a stranger who had faked a pregnancy

contacts.what_institution_did: Called a Code Pink and searched, but waited about an hour, holding a senior-staff meeting about its liability, before calling authorities.
contacts.quote: they waited one hour to call the authorities. They decided to call an emergency board meeting or some type of meeting with their senior staff
contacts.what_happened_next: Police/FBI alerted about two hours after the abduction.
contacts.notes: Next segment: 'because they knew they had a huge problem. They had a potential lawsuit on their hands' (11:45).

contacts.institution: Oklahoma City police, then the FBI
contacts.what_institution_did: FBI took the case, ran daily press appeals and a tip line.
contacts.quote: The FBI came to my parents' room in the early hours of June 21st, and they explained the typical process for families after their child goes missing.

contacts.what_was_asked: tip from a man who worked at Hardee's
contacts.what_institution_did: Followed up, exposed a forged birth certificate, got a confession and arrested the abductor.
contacts.quote: So once they pointed that fact out, she eventually confessed to everything. At 11 p.m. on June 30th, she was arrested.
contacts.what_happened_next: Baby identified and returned.

contacts.what_institution_did: Took her to hospital, identified her by footprints and records.
contacts.quote: The social worker came to pick me up and took me to the local hospital there. They identified me with footprints and medical records and said I was in good health

contacts.what_institution_did: Abductor pleaded guilty to kidnapping; five years plus probation.
contacts.quote: She was sentenced to five years in prison or 60 months and three years probation with further mental care after her release.
contacts.what_happened_next: Parents were very unhappy with the sentence.

contacts.what_institution_did: Waived birth costs and provided free therapy to her parents.
contacts.quote: The hospital compensated my birth. They didn't have to pay for that. So there's that. They did provide free therapy for them after I came home, which helped.
contacts.what_happened_next: She chose not to sue the hospital before 19.

persons.outcome_quote: it's not every day that a kidnapped 11-day-old baby is found and returned home safely and in good health.
persons.decisive_work_quote: he thought it was weird that the baby on TV, baby Whitney, and the baby she was passing off as her own, both had a full head of hair with a curl on top.
persons.notes: harmed_by_institution_ever set true because the hospital's lapse and one-hour delay endangered her. Decisive work: the tipster recognised her from TV coverage, also motivated by her grandfather's $10,000 reward (23:09); the FBI organised the coverage, so 'institution' is a close alternative. Archival news audio of her mother's appeal is played; the show cites news archives and she cites court documents.

persons.name: Teresa

contacts.what_institution_did: Five-year sentence; as a 'third party' she could not sue the hospital.
contacts.quote: My parents were considered a third party, so they couldn't bring a lawsuit against Deaconess Hospital.
contacts.what_happened_next: Hospital provided free therapy.

persons.outcome_quote: it's not every day that a kidnapped 11-day-old baby is found and returned home safely and in good health.

coder_notes: All 12 chunk files read to their last line (22 episodes, S13 E1-E22). INDEX.txt read; two unassigned episodes opened (neither concerns a season 13 story). The other INDEX entries are general Data Points topics, a crossover (Caitlin Mathis, Texas) and a promo, with no indication they continue a season 13 story, so they were not opened. Perpetrator names and pseudonyms are replaced with [perpetrator] in quotations; third parties are described by role. Judgment calls: Whitney's mother (Teresa) is recorded as a co-victim; Natalia's earlier abusive ex is a separate, thin record. Three women harmed by the same perpetrators are recorded from secondhand accounts (Birdie's abuser's former employee and two women in Arya's story), at low confidence. Madison (Odessa's story) is coded never_reached; a lead pastor's general caution to the perpetrator was not a report of harm. In several stories (Zoe, Sage, Birdie) medical contacts where the harm was not disclosed are noted in notes, not coded as contacts. Odessa is coded harmed_by_institution because a couples therapist told her to make herself sexually available to her abuser.
